instructions: Rinse the rice in a medium pot with cold water, swirling and draining until the water runs almost clear. Add 1 3/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered until you serve.

Drain the tofu. Cut each block crosswise into 4 slabs, then cut each slab in half to make 8 rectangles about 1/2 inch thick, 16 in all. Lay them on a clean towel, pat them dry, and sprinkle both sides with the salt. Leave them for 10 minutes, then pat them dry again.
Meanwhile, slice the 4 green onions thin and mince the garlic. In a small bowl, whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, green onions, garlic and sesame seeds until the sugar dissolves.

Heat 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add 8 tofu slices in one layer. Leave them alone for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is deep golden and lets go of the pan.
Flip the slices and cook for 3 minutes, until golden on the second side. Transfer them to a platter and spoon half the sauce over them while they're hot.
Wipe out the skillet, heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil, and repeat with the other 8 slices and the rest of the sauce.
Taste a slice. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice. Put the gochugaru on the table for the adults.
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings (Asian Supper has 3.7 from 7, below 4.0), and the trusted-cook site has no dubu buchim, so this is a fallback led by Ramen Rater's soy, vinegar and scallion sauce, which matches the list's description. Pan-fried slices of firm tofu, salted and dried, then sauced hot, is what every version does. Ramen Rater presses the tofu for 30 minutes; here it's salted and dried for 10 to fit 30 minutes, the same idea Asian Supper uses. Its 1 tsp of gochugaru is moved to the table so the base stays mild. Scaled from 1 block to 2 for a dinner with rice.
